core.title: Give every wagon a declared, stable URN and its documented wagon directory layout
core.given: The change creates or modifies a wagon, meaning its defining manifest or its own file set, wherever it is located. Files that merely mention a wagon do not count.
core.when: The planner creates, edits, renames, moves or reorganises that wagon.
core.then: The wagon declares a stable URN, and that URN does not change when the wagon is edited, renamed or moved.
prefer: Keep a wagon's existing URN when you edit, rename or move it.
Give a new wagon a URN in the grammar defined by planner.wagon.urn-naming.

Place every wagon under the wagon directory given by the profile's wagon-directory pattern, with the documented wagon file layout. This placement is required by the same statement as the URN obligation and is a mandatory part of this rule. Derive the wagon's directory name (its slug) as planner.wagon.logical-vs-filesystem-naming specifies.
avoid: A wagon with no declared URN, or with a URN derived from something that changes over time.
Rewriting a wagon's URN as part of other edits.
A wagon that lives outside the wagon directory given by the profile, or whose file set departs from the documented layout.
core.why: Trains and components refer to a wagon by its URN, and the URN must resolve to a real wagon at a predictable location. A missing or changing URN, or a misplaced wagon, breaks those references.
evidence: Each wagon touched by the change declares exactly one URN (in its defining manifest), and for an existing wagon that URN is the same before and after the change.
Each wagon touched by the change lives under the wagon directory given by the profile, and its file set matches the documented layout. This is a mandatory part of this rule.
verification: Disposition: documentation-only, severity 3. This is a review guideline, not a strict gate; a reviewer confirms compliance by inspection, and no automated gate is implied.

Unit of check: the wagon, not each associated file. A wagon is identified by its defining manifest, the file that declares the wagon. Check the URN once per wagon on that definition, and check the layout on the wagon's own file set. Do not treat docs, trains or components that only reference a wagon URN as wagons.

The plan root is a discovery hint only and must never restrict detection: a wagon definition found outside the expected wagon directory is still found and reported as a layout violation. Identification is content-based and works wherever the definition sits.

Observability gaps: a classifier for wagon definitions is needed, and until one exists an LLM judges; a diff-level observer is needed to compare the declared URN before and after a change and to compare the wagon's file set with the documented layout, and until it exists an LLM judges.

values: wagon definition (the file that defines it, typically its manifest)
file of a wagon's own file set
wagon URN declared, changed or removed
wagon's own files added, removed or relocated

fires: A planner creates a new wagon, wherever its definition is placed.
A planner edits, renames or moves an existing wagon, or edits its declared URN.
A planner adds, removes or relocates files of a wagon's own file set. This includes a layout-only change.
A wagon definition is found outside the wagon directory given by the profile.
A wagon definition has no declared URN.
doesNotFire: A file only describes or references a wagon, for example a doc, train or component that cites a wagon URN, and no wagon definition or wagon file set is created, moved or modified.
The change touches only non-wagon artifacts, such as source code, tests, or plan artifacts that define no wagon.

profileRequirements.meaning: The directory in which every wagon must live, and the pattern against which a wagon's own file set is judged for layout; the core's placement, avoid and evidence items refer to this pattern.
The root of plan artifacts, used only as a discovery hint for finding wagon definitions; it must never act as a required filter.

neutralityNotes: Nothing in the agent-facing items is stack-mechanical, so bunOnly is empty: the only concrete values (the plan root and the plan/<wagon-slug>/ wagon directory) are supplied through the closed-vocabulary keys layout.wagon_dir and roots.plan. 'Wagon' is kept as a structural concept rather than a stack name: the vocabulary itself defines it (layout.wagon_dir, 'a bounded slice of the product') and the wagon is the subject of the obligation. The activation fact kind path_glob has no neutral counterpart among the allowed fact kinds, so its semantics (plan root as a discovery hint that must never restrict detection) moved to core:verification with the path from roots.plan; detection is neither weakened nor broadened. The 'documented file layout' of a wagon's file set stays a deferral to the ruleset's wagon-layout documentation, exactly as bun.json defers it; no profile key describes a wagon's internal file set and the Bun rule does not enumerate one either, so no key is proposed. References to sibling conventions (planner.wagon.urn-naming, planner.wagon.logical-vs-filesystem-naming) are ruleset-level rather than stack-level and are kept so the obligation is not weakened. Sidecar term ids (wagon_urn, wagon_layout) and non-agent-facing metadata (audit, splitSuggestion, additions, trace) stay with the Bun realization; the splitSuggestion planner.wagon.layout is realization metadata and the layout obligation remains mandatory and unconditional here.
